title: About
text:
I’m Sean Plummer, an applied mathematician/statistician working on:

singular learning theory and Bayesian asymptotics

geometry-aware variational inference

fairness in statistical and machine learning models

statistical principles for understanding and evaluating LLMs — from generalization and uncertainty to fairness and reliability

This site, Asymptotically Correct, is named after our grad school trivia team and doubles as my evolving research notebook.

title: Projects
text:
A non-exhaustive subset of things I’m thinking about:

Thermodynamic SLT — phase transitions, finite-temperature corrections, singular fluctuation.

Geometry-aware VI — SIVI, structured VI, α-VB, and SLT-inspired risk bounds.

Global fairness — invariance-based fairness functionals and counterexamples to local criteria.

Spatial & network models — SDM-CAR priors, AME models, and scalable inference.

NLP / LLMs — RAG, evaluation, and fairness / reliability in HR analytics.

title: Real Log Canonical Thresholds (RLCT)
text:
Real Log Canonical Thresholds (RLCT)
This page will collect notes on the Real Log Canonical Threshold (RLCT),
a central quantity in Singular Learning Theory governing the asymptotic behavior of the marginal likelihood and free energy.
Topics to be added:

definition of RLCT via zeta functions

basic examples (mixtures, reduced rank regression, neural networks)

connection to learning coefficients

role in generalization error and asymptotic expansions

More details coming soon.

title: Zeta Functions and Singularities
text:
Zeta Functions in Singular Learning Theory
This page will collect definitions and examples of the zeta function
[ (z) = K(w)^z (w),dw, ] which plays a key role in determining the RLCT and generalizing the notion of model complexity in singular learning settings.
Topics to be added:

definition and analytic continuation

poles and their multiplicities

relationship with the RLCT

examples from mixture models and low-rank models

More notes coming soon.

title: Resolution of Singularities
text:
Resolution of Singularities
This page will summarize the basic tools from algebraic geometry used
to analyze singular statistical models via resolution maps.
Topics to be added:

blow-ups and local coordinates

how resolution simplifies the Kullback–Leibler landscape

Jacobian factors and transformed likelihood

the role of resolution in computing the RLCT

simple illustrative examples

More details will be filled in as the notes develop.

title: Asymptotically Correct
text:
Welcome to Asymptotically Correct — my long-form research notebook.
I use this site to collect:

working notes on singular learning theory (SLT) and its thermodynamic view

experiments in variational inference (SIVI, structured VI, α-VB, etc.)

work on fair learning

applied and computational notes in NLP / LLMs / RAG

All content on this site reflects ongoing research in draft form. No statement, proof, or claim should be interpreted as finalized, peer-reviewed, or guaranteed to be correct.
